text:
tejas: Heads-up 1: customer incident where an on-call operator used a long-lived org-admin API key as a 'breakglass' during outage, and that key later got used for config changes in tenant projects. They want stronger guardrails.

marta: yikes. breakglass shouldn't be a regular API key. We should treat breakglass as an auditable, short-lived, operator-only flow with explicit approval.

owen: existing problem: engineers use standard org API keys and toggle feature flags. No MFA, no one-time justification memo.

lia: proposal: introduce "emergency tokens" flow: - generated via Console/CLI with a required justification string - ephemeral TTL 10m by default - signed by HSM and single-use enforced by token revocation list - requires 2nd approver for org-scoped operations

tejas: agree. also need strong scoping: emergency token must carry a reason and list of allowed api routes (deny-by-default). If the operator requests wildcard access we should force a separate breakglass with stricter audit.

marta: how enforce? middleware can verify token claim emergency==true and check JTI against single-use ledger (redis). If JTI seen before reject. For Dedicated/Private, ledger must be pluggable (redis or filesystem) so air-gapped installs work.

owen: audit side: every emergency action should create an immutable audit record: operator, approver, justification, signed request payload, and HSM-signed audit receipt returned to operator. That way customer can submit receipts for compliance.

lia: UX: Console modal prompts: "Are you sure? Provide justification." show affected routes and estimated impact. CLI: `redwood emergency --reason "DB failover" --allow routes:/v1/*` which returns token and receipt.

marta: edge-case: what about automation that legitimately needs emergency-like privileges (runbooks)? We should support machine principals that can request emergency tokens via a registered runbook workflow with pre-approved justification templates and shortened TTL. Those requests still require operator approval or pre-authorized automation with a signing key.

tejas: question: do we treat emergency tokens as org-scoped only, or allow project-scoped emergency tokens?

owen: allow project-scoped by default. org-scoped emergency tokens require stricter approval (2 human approvers and account owner confirmation).

sec-bot: security-scan: found 4 API routes with no explicit allowlist for emergency flow. See https://ci.internal/scan/4771112222

lia: enforcement detail: policy engine must ignore emergency==true when evaluating normal RBAC unless the policy explicitly permits emergency_principals. Otherwise emergency could bypass policy unintentionally. We should add explicit predicate `is_emergency()` in policy language.
marta: policy example:

  // safe default
  deny if is_emergency() == true && not allow_emergency(resource, action);

  // opt-in example
  allow if is_emergency() && allow_emergency(resource, action) && operator_approved();

tejas: migration note: we must scan existing policies that implicitly assume admin keys (e.g., allow if actor.org == resource.owner). Scanner should flag these for manual review.

ops-bot: scheduled policy-scan job: emergency-safety-patterns -> https://ci.internal/policy-scan/4771112222 (ETA 1h)

marta: implementation plan: 1) token minting service + HSM signature + single-use ledger (owen) 2) UI/CLI emergency path + receipts (lia) 3) policy language predicate + linter rules (marta) 4) Dedicated/Private deployment docs + pluggable ledger adapter (tejas)

owen: timeline: prototype 2w (internal-only), pilot with SRE in 4w, public beta in 8w.

lia: telemetry: emit metric emergency_token_issued{scope=org|project}, emergency_actions_total, emergency_rejects_total and provide a dashboard. Also tag audit events with receipt_id for search.
tejas: add a blocker: ensure HSM keys used for signing are rotated and access-controlled. For Private, support customer-managed KMS.

marta: security checklist: - enforce MFA for human approvers - require approver not be the requestor - limit session IP ranges optionally - capture pre/post snapshots for risky resources (feature flags, routing rules)

sec-bot: created ticket AUTH-4512: emergency token flow + audit receipts https://tickets.internal/AUTH-4512

owen: one more thought: we need to prevent replay via logs. Don't log full token; only log receipt_id and redacted token id. receipts contain signed hash of action that can be independently verified.

lia: customer communication: we'll announce change as "managed breakglass" feature. For customers on Private we provide migration docs and an optional compatibility mode for 30 days where both flows work, but we log a deprecation notice.
tejas: ok. assign owners: owens -> minting service, lia -> UX + receipts, marta -> policy + linter, tejas -> deployment + KMS docs. We'll reconvene after RFC draft. :thumbsup:\"
